name: Hermes Agent
version_context: NousResearch/hermes-agent commit db1fa153fe24a051af44ef8ee862b93e27998060 (official main revision resolved 2026-10-24)
summary: A Python agent and gateway system from Nous Research combining a terminal conversation loop, tool execution, context compression, persistent memory and skills, delegation, scheduled jobs, and multi-platform messaging backends.
scope: cron scheduling, gateway, and messaging integrations

features.name: Multi-surface conversation and tool loop
features.description: The official README describes a full TUI and a gateway for Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and other surfaces; the fixed conversation loop assembles requests, handles model responses, dispatches tool rounds, retries/fallbacks, and finalizes turns.
benefits: One agent runtime can serve terminal and messaging workflows
Streaming, interruption, tool output, and retry behavior are centralized in the turn loop
costs: Many surfaces create input, delivery, and lifecycle variations
A large loop must coordinate provider, tool, context, and gateway policies

features.name: Context compression, memory, and skills learning loop
features.description: Hermes includes automatic context compression with protected head/tail and summary routes, memory-provider fan-out with egress scrubbing and bounded calls, and skill-index delta notes that update available skills without rebuilding a cached prompt prefix.
benefits: Supports long-lived conversations and cross-session recall
Keeps changing skills visible while preserving prompt-cache structure
Memory provider calls have explicit redaction and admission controls
costs: Summaries and memory are lossy or asynchronous projections
Multiple context and provider policies increase consistency surface
Background calls and caches require bounded-failure handling

features.name: Fail-closed delegation and tool execution boundaries
features.description: Delegation providers are selected from a normalized registry and unavailable configured backends return tool errors rather than silently switching routes; tool execution has sequential/concurrent dispatch, guardrails, persisted-result handling, and a common result projection.
benefits: Preserves configured routing intent under provider failure
Centralizes tool-call identity, result shape, and safety checks
costs: Fail-closed behavior can stop work when a configured backend is unavailable
Concurrent tools require ordering, cancellation, and large-result memory policies

features.name: Scheduled automation through a gateway
features.description: The official README documents a built-in cron scheduler and gateway, while the fixed scheduler uses a tick lock, tracks in-flight jobs, handles stale gateway/code conditions, routes jobs, and delivers outcomes to configured platforms.
benefits: Runs unattended jobs with platform delivery
Makes recurring agent work a first-class runtime surface
costs: Scheduling introduces overlap, liveness, stale-code, and delivery failure states
Background execution expands credential and authorization boundaries

mathematical_views.question: How do user input, model responses, tool rounds, compression, retries, interruptions, and finalization advance a Hermes turn?
assumptions: A turn is an ordered transcript plus provider/tool runtime state
Tool calls may execute sequentially or concurrently and produce one projected result shape
Retries and fallback routes are policy transitions, not guaranteed success
The view abstracts network providers and platform delivery

mathematical_views.model: Lossy context and memory projection system
mathematical_views.question: How do compression summaries, retained transcript regions, memory providers, and skill-index notes affect the context seen by later model calls?
assumptions: Compression maps a transcript to a bounded prompt projection
Memory and skill notes are auxiliary projections with explicit scrubbing or delta semantics
Asynchronous providers can be delayed, skipped, or bounded by admission controls
No projection is treated as a proof of semantic equivalence to the original history

mathematical_views.question: Which job, ownership, liveness, route, execution, and delivery states permit a cron tick to run or defer work?
assumptions: Ticks contend on a lock and jobs have persisted definitions and in-flight state
A stale process may yield to a fresh gateway under the scheduler policy
Delivery and execution are separate transitions with failure records
The model abstracts operating-system locking and platform APIs

benefits: Shared behavior across TUI and messaging

costs: Lossy/asynchronous projections need consistency and failure policies

benefits: Configured routes are not silently bypassed
costs: Unavailable backends can block delegated work
Scheduler liveness, overlap, and delivery states add operational burden
